The authors of this paper are Fengqing Jiang, Zhangchen Xu, Luyao Niu, Zhen Xiang, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Bo Li, and Radha Poovend

Sure, here is the summary for the Summary of Attack Methods section:

The paper proposes a novel jailbreak attack, called ArtPrompt, which exploits the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in recognizing ASCII art. The attack consists of two steps: (1) finding words within a prompt that may trigger rejections from LLMs, and (2) crafting cloaked prompts by visually encoding the identified words using ASCII art. The attack only requires black-box access to the victim LLMs, making it a practical attack. The authors evaluate ArtPrompt on five state-of-the-art LLMs and show that it can effectively and efficiently induce undesired behaviors from all five models. The paper also introduces a benchmark, named Vision-in-Text Challenge (VITC), to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics. The results indicate that all five LLMs struggle to understand input queries that use ASCII art to represent one single letter or number, and the ability of the LLMs to correctly recognize input queries drops significantly as the input queries contain more letters or numbers.

section: Introduction to the Mechanism of Success
content:
Sure, here is the summary for the Introduction to the Mechanism of Success:

The paper "ASCII Art-based Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned LLMs" introduces a novel jailbreak attack that exploits the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in recognizing ASCII art. The authors develop a benchmark, Vision-in-Text Challenge (VITC), to evaluate the capabilities of five state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, and Llama2) in perceiving and responding to queries in the form of ASCII art. The results show that all five LLMs struggle to understand input queries that use ASCII art to represent one single letter or number, and their ability to correctly recognize input queries drops significantly as the input queries contain more letters or numbers. The authors use this observation to develop the ArtPrompt attack, which leverages the poor performance of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from LLMs. The attack only requires black-box access to the victim LLMs, making it a practical attack.

Sure, here is the summary for the Related Work section:

Related Work:

The paper discusses the related work in the field of jailbreaking large language models (LLMs) using ASCII art-based attacks. The authors mention previous work on safety alignment of LLMs, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and red-teaming. They highlight the limitations of these approaches, which focus exclusively on the semantics of natural language involved in training/instruction corpora, overlooking the fact that corpora can be interpreted in multiple ways beyond just semantics.
